_meta.question: salted per-class Lloyd-Max codebooks vs one global codebook at equal bits/weight
_meta.parity_note: bits/weight = log2(k) in every arm (k=4/8/16 at 2/3/4 bits, identical across arms). The salt-class index is derived from weight position (free side information per the spec), not stored per weight, so the salted arm's N*k total entries do NOT cost extra bits per weight. Entry-count parity is intentionally NOT imposed on total entries; parity is imposed on codebook size k and on the Lloyd-Max procedure.
_meta.lloyd_max: 1-D Lloyd k-means, per-cluster mean update, deterministic equal-percentile init (np.percentile at (i+0.5)/k quantiles), <=20 iters, 1e-9 relative early stop, centroids sorted; fit float64, quantize float32
_meta.subsample: codebooks fit on rows r%65==0 (65%64==1 -> sampled rows cover every row-class residue mod 64 exactly; ~1/65 of tensor, 15k-305k samples/class), EXCEPT 5120-row tensors with a row salt use rows r%17==0 (review fix #3: down L63 was fit-noise-dominated at r%65 — probe: r%65 1.1330 / r%33 1.0623 / all-rows 0.9973; r%17 = 301 rows, 4-5 rows/class, gcd(17,64)==1 so all residues still covered); global book fit on the union of the same subsample; MSE and per-class max error computed exactly over the FULL tensor. Per-class absmax tables and per-class fit-sample counts are persisted per tensor in this JSON.
_meta.salted_scale: spec 2-step (mechanism REPLACED per review #1): per-class scale = absmax over the FULL tensor (exact streaming max); ONE shared k-entry codebook fit on the union of all classes normalized by their own absmax; recon = shared_centroid * class_scale; k + N total entries (full entry-count parity with the global arm's k-entry book)
_meta.salted_scale_history: the ORIGINAL variant (per-class books fit on w/absmax) was a mathematical no-op: Lloyd-Max with the mean update is scale-equivariant, lloyd_max(x/s)*s == lloyd_max(x), so per-class normalized books were provably identical to raw per-class books and r_ss == r_s was forced by construction (measured ~1e-9 agreement on all 27 cells). The replacement is the distinct 2-step mechanism the spec intended.
_meta.max_error_note: measured on the pre-fix sweep: salted per-class MAX error is LOWER than global in 14/27 cells (lm_head 4-bit 0.258 vs 0.304, 1.18x lower) — Task 4 must NOT repeat the blanket no-max-error-win claim; see class_max_err_salted vs max_abs_err_global per cell
_meta.negative_scales: ~50.7% of weight_scale entries are negative (AutoRound); dequant path multiplies the signed scale (reused from heterogeneity.py), absmax class scale is sign-agnostic
